text:
maya: Heads up — noticed a bunch of traces with missing child spans starting ~10:12 UTC after the fanout exporter change. Parent spans exist but a lot of leaf spans are gone. Anyone else seeing this?

henry: yep saw it too. tracedown dashboard shows a spike in partial traces ~10:12-10:30. looks correlated with the new exporter added to the fanout group.

jon: interesting — could be backpressure on the exporter queue causing early drop on flush. do we have exporter logs?

maya: pasted a couple of excerpts from the collector logs:
```
2026-03-20T10:12:15.432Z WARN exporter_queue_full exporter=fanout-worker-7 dropped_spans=134 reason="max_queue_size"
2026-03-20T10:12:15.433Z INFO flusher started batch_size=64 exporter=fanout-worker-7
2026-03-20T10:12:15.434Z ERROR flusher_flush_failed exporter=fanout-worker-7 err="context canceled"
```

lisa: @jon @henry looks like the fanout path tries to write to all exporters in parallel and uses the global queue size. when one exporter hits backpressure we seem to trim the whole batch instead of retrying per-exporter.

jon: if that's true we introduced a regression when wiring the shared queue. older behavior was per-exporter queue + per-exporter backoff. now it's a shared queue + optimistic fanout.

maya: repro steps I ran in staging: spin up three exporters, one intentionally rate-limited (nginx rate_limit), then bulk-send traces. result: collector logs show queue saturation and `dropped_spans` for whole batches.

henry: can we confirm whether sampling happens before or after fanout? if sampling removes children after fanout we could create orphans.

lisa: sampling is upstream (pre-export), so this is not sampling-induced. looks like the race is: flush decides batch -> enqueues to shared queue -> one exporter blocks -> queue full -> flush errors out and increments dropped counter for the batch. children never reach storage.

tracing-bot: detected anomaly: partial_trace_rate up 4.9x at 10:12 UTC. top affected service: route-router-prod. traces with trace_id prefix 0x8f3b show >60% missing child spans.

jon: quick mitigation: revert the fanout shared-queue change or change fanout to do per-exporter enqueue with independent backpressure handling. which is faster?

maya: deploying a revert now. @deploy-bot can you roll back commit c7a9f3 (fanout: shared queue)?

deploy-bot: rollback triggered by maya for commit c7a9f3 on branch main — rollout started.

henry: temporary workaround if rollback takes time: increase shared queue size and enable exporter-level timeouts so blocked exporters fail fast rather than clog the queue. but that's a bandaid.

lisa: agree, bandaid only. also we should add metrics for per-exporter enqueue latency + per-exporter drop counts. current `exporter_dropped_spans_total` is at the fanout level and hides which exporter caused the problem.

jon: action items I can take: 1) revert PR and redeploy (maya doing), 2) add per-exporter counters + per-exporter queue depth metric, 3) add e2e test that simulates one slow exporter under fanout.

maya: thanks — will post when rollback completes. tagging infra oncall if rollback fails.

tracing-bot: rollback completed: deploy c7a9f3 reverted at 10:17:12 UTC.

maya: rollback done. early look at traces shows partial_trace_rate back to baseline. still want to keep the per-exporter metrics change — opening a follow-up PR.

henry: let's also add a dashboard panel that surfaces partial_trace_rate and top exporters with dropped spans. helpful for runbooks.

lisa: also consider retention impact — we accidentally flagged some traces as partial and retention TTL logic dropped them earlier than usual because they lacked key spans. we should check whether retention decisions were triggered for any affected traces.

jon: good point. check storage logs for TTL deletions between 10:12-10:40. if we find any, we need to run a short restore window.

maya: created ticket INF-2321 with logs + example trace_ids and assigned follow-ups (per-exporter metrics, e2e test, retention audit). link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2321

lisa: nice. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

jon: after INF-2321 we should update rollout docs — fanout changes must require perf + backpressure review. learned the hard way.

henry: agreed.
